# Acme Payments Code Review Rules (payments-service)

## HTTP Clients & Retries

**ADR-006: All HTTP calls must use `make_client()` instead of direct requests/httpx imports** — Provides 3s connect timeout, 10s read timeout, 2 retries with jittered backoff on connect errors and 502/503/504, request-id propagation, and metrics; exception: provider SDKs like Stripe manage their own transport — Adopted February 23, 2026 (ADR-006) after February 11, 2026 incident where requests.get() without timeout hung worker threads for 9 minutes — Enforced in PR #110, #113, #123, #127

**No multiple retry layers** — Shared client handles transient errors, nightly jobs are outer retry, additional backoff loops forbidden; prevents retry storms where layers multiply attempts — Motivated by INC-12 (February 2026) where stacking retry layers caused 15 attempts per charge against card network — Enforced in PR #123 (alice rejected frank's exponential backoff suggestion)

**All outbound HTTP must go through client modules in app/clients/ built on `make_client`** — No inline httpx.post() calls; ensures consistent timeouts, retries, request IDs — Enforced in PR #127

## Money Representation

**ADR-007: Money stored as integer minor units (amount_cents: int + currency: str ISO 4217), never Decimal or float** — Fields named *_cents regardless of currency exponent; no Decimal or float in app/ directory — Prevents JSON serialization inconsistencies, rounding mismatches with Stripe/banks for JPY/KWD currencies, bugs from Decimal+float mixing — Adopted March 10-11, 2026 (PR #112), supersedes earlier Decimal guidance from PR #103, #106 — Enforced in PR #118, #130

**Percentage calculations use integer arithmetic with explicit rounding helpers** — apply_bps and round_half_even_div from app.domain.money for all percentage-based fees; reject inline percentage math like `amount * 29 // 1000` — Ensures consistent rounding in exactly one place, preventing ad-hoc rounding choices — Confirmed March 11, 2026 (ADR-007, PR #112)

**Display formatting only in API response schemas** — Keep integer minor units through business logic, format only at API boundary — Part of ADR-007

## Architectural Patterns (ADRs)

**ADR-003: Thin API handlers** — Handlers in app/api/ validate input, call one service function, map results; no DB sessions or queries in handlers; services get session through app.db.session_scope(); queries live in app/repos/ — Services reusable from jobs/workers/CLI, not just HTTP; prevents duplicated query logic — Motivated by two December 2025 refund bugs from 150+ line handlers mixing parsing, SQL, and provider calls — Adopted January 8, 2026 (PR #101) — Enforced in PR #104, #117, #122, #125

**ADR-003 exception: Health and metrics endpoints can touch infrastructure directly** — Added April 2, 2026; operational endpoints exist to test infrastructure itself, not business logic — alice rejected carol's suggestion to add service layer to /healthz in PR #116

**Directory layout convention** — app/api/ for FastAPI routers, app/services/ for business logic, app/repos/ for SQLAlchemy persistence, app/domain/ for domain types, app/clients/ for external integrations — Documented in CONTRIBUTING.md, confirmed May 12, 2026

**ADR-004: All money-moving POST endpoints require @idempotent decorator** — Endpoints must require Idempotency-Key header; missing key returns 400; duplicates replay cached response (24h TTL in Redis) — Prevents duplicate operations from client retries — Motivated by January 2026 duplicate EUR 1,240 refund when mobile app retried timed-out request — Adopted February 4-6, 2026 (PR #107) — Enforced in PR #111, #125, #130

**ADR-004 exception: Provider webhooks dedupe on provider event id, not Idempotency-Key** — Webhooks (e.g., Stripe) don't carry custom headers but providers supply unique event IDs; deduplication uses processed_events.claim table — alice rejected dan's suggestion to add @idempotent to webhook endpoint in PR #119 (April 22, 2026)

**ADR-005: Pydantic restricted to API boundaries** — Pydantic models only in app/api/schemas.py and app/config.py; domain and service types must be frozen dataclasses with slots=True in app/domain/; conversion happens once in handlers — Prevents Pydantic v2 coercion silently converting strings to numbers; validation ran multiple times per request in refund path (15% of request time) — Adopted February 18, 2026 (PR #109) after coercion bug in capture path in early February 2026 — Enforced in PR #115, #124

**ADR-008: Expand/contract pattern for database migrations** — Migrations must work with both currently deployed and new code; column renames/drops follow expand→write both→backfill→switch reads→contract sequence in separate PRs; PRs dropping/renaming columns cannot include application code changes — Prevents crashes during rolling deployments — Motivated by INC-19 (May 7, 2026) where dropping charges.legacy_status in same deploy as code changes caused 6 minutes of crashes — Adopted May 12, 2026 (PR #121) — Enforced in PR #128

**Services must raise domain errors (app.errors), not HTTPException** — API layer maps domain errors to HTTP status codes; services called from consumers, jobs, workers, CLI where HTTP semantics don't apply — alice enforced in PR #117 (errors.Conflict instead of HTTPException(409)), PR #127, PR #124

## Coding Conventions

**Use clock.now() from app.utils.clock instead of datetime.utcnow()** — Tests use frozen_clock fixture which freezes time to deterministic date (January 15, 2026 12:00), preventing test failures across midnight boundaries; utcnow() returns naive datetime while DB timestamp fields are timezone-aware, causing type mismatches — bob enforced in PR #105, carol in PR #120

**Logging: constant snake_case event names with keyword arguments, not f-strings** — Documented in app/utils/logging.py; enables Datadog event grouping and monitoring; f-strings prevent log grouping and require regex-parsing — Established March 23, 2026 (bob, alice, carol) — carol enforced in PR #129

**All log content with customer data must use redact() to protect PII** — Enforced for all new log lines — Established March 24, 2026 (alice) — Enforced in PR #114, #124

**All environment variable reads added to Settings class, not os.environ directly** — Ensures visibility in config docs, prevents test crashes from missing variables at import time, maintains PAYMENTS_ prefix convention — bob enforced in PR #122 (May 13, 2026)

**Exception: scripts/ directory exempt from Settings and structured logging** — One-off scripts under scripts/ may use os.environ and print statements; scripts run manually from bastion with different DATABASE_URL values; importing app.config would unnecessarily pull in all app settings and validation — alice and carol established June 10, 2026 in PR #126

**Import ordering handled exclusively by automated tooling** — ruff with isort in pre-commit hooks and CI; reviewers must not manually review or request changes to import order — alice rejected frank's manual import reordering in PR #105, #117; carol rejected in PR #129

## Documentation

**Only public service functions require docstrings; private helpers (underscore-prefixed) self-documenting** — Name and implementation considered sufficient documentation for private helpers; tests serve as better documentation; docstrings on helpers tend to rot — Established in PR #102 (carol), enforced in PR #104 (bob), #122, #129 (dan rejected frank's suggestion)

**Test naming format: test_<unit>__<scenario>__<expected>** — Example: test_refund__exceeds_capture__raises_refund_exceeds_capture; test name alone should indicate what broke when it fails in CI — Documented in CONTRIBUTING.md — bob enforced in PR #106

**Tests use factories from tests/factories.py, not inline model construction** — Use make_charge, etc.; prevents inconsistent fake implementations (previously had six different fake charge implementations) — Documented in CONTRIBUTING.md — bob enforced in PR #106

**No type annotations in test files** — mypy excludes tests/ directory in pyproject.toml; fixture types add noise without real safety benefit — carol and bob consensus — frank's suggestions rejected in PR #111, #125, #128

**Migration guidelines documented in CONTRIBUTING.md, not only ADRs** — Team members don't read ADRs before writing migrations, need discoverable location — bob added section May 11, 2026 per alice's request in PR #121

**ADR-writing convention: start strict without pre-emptive exceptions; add exceptions only when need is concrete** — alice and bob adopted January 6-7, 2026; example: health endpoint exemption from ADR-003 deferred until endpoint existed

## Workflow & Tooling

**Developer workflow: install pre-commit hooks for ruff lint/format on every commit, run make test for pytest with coverage** — Documented in CONTRIBUTING.md

**No hard line limits for functions** — Split functions only when hard to read, not based on line count; prioritize cohesion and readability over arbitrary limits — frank's suggestion to split 30-line function rejected by carol and dan in PR #120 (April 29, 2026)

## Domain-Specific Rules

**Fraud scoring: decline charges scoring 80+ on fraud-scoring service /v2/score** — Decline with PaymentDeclined("fraud_score_too_high") before payment authorization — Threshold agreed with risk team March 12, 2026 — Dan's PR #113 (March 16-18, 2026)

**Card display details retrieved from tokenizer service, never stored in payments-service database** — Security and compliance requirement to avoid storing sensitive payment card data locally — carol confirmed May 13, 2026 in PR #122

**Financial calculations validated against historical data from finance department before merging** — Ensures accuracy — Dan validated FX conversions against 200 conversions from finance spreadsheet in PR #118 (April 15, 2026)
